teaser.text: Marriott International sells a way to make money from hotels without owning most of the buildings. It puts its brands, booking network, loyalty program, and operating expertise between travelers, hotel owners, developers, and banks, then collects fees as money moves through the system.

stock.meta_description: Marriott's forecast gives a probability-weighted value of $399.44 in October 2029, with bear, base and bull cases.
stock.opening: Marriott's weighted value is $399.44 in October 2029, implying a 6% gain. Marriott's forecast turns on whether Marriott can expand its fee engine without borrowing away the cash that supports shareholder returns.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how Marriott's business works, who its rivals are, how management runs it, and what risks could change the outlook.

paragraphs.text: The forecast points to modest expected returns, with substantial downside if travel weakens and considerable upside if Marriott converts its pipeline successfully. The probability-weighted price is $363.95 in October 2027, equal to a 5% loss including dividends. It rises to $381.43 in October 2028, a 1% gain, and $399.44 in October 2029, a 6% gain.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Marriott?

paragraphs.text: The base case requires successful openings to turn roughly 265,000 rooms under construction at year-end 2025 into recurring fees and operating-profit growth. Signed projects still face financing, renovation, and demand hurdles. The downside grows if regional weakness or owner cost pressure slows fees while distributions exceed free cash flow. Marriott’s next scheduled catalyst is its third-quarter report on November 2, 2026, when investors will test guidance against RevPAR, room growth, and card-fee contribution.

The bull case gives $482.43 initially and $652.59 finally, a 72% total return. Its 15% probability reflects the need for stronger demand, healthy owners, fast pipeline conversion, rising card fees and sustained buybacks to occur together. Roughly 265,000 rooms under construction provide opportunity, but signed rooms do not guarantee openings.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Marriott really make?

paragraphs.text: Net income of $2,601 million became operating cash flow of $3,212 million in 2025. After the investment deduction used here, free cash flow was $2,258 million. Deducting $236 million of stock-based pay produces an analytical “real free cash flow” figure, because shares given to employees transfer value even when they preserve cash at first.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Marriott today?

paragraphs.text: A trailing P/E of 40.0x means investors pay $40 for each dollar of earnings per share from the past year. The forward P/E of 29.4x uses expected earnings, so it assumes profits will rise. Buybacks can raise earnings per share without raising total profit: if $1 billion of earnings is divided among 100 million shares, each share earns $10; after 10 million shares are bought back, each remaining share earns about $11.11.

blocks.heading: Does Marriott's dividend fit its free cash flow?

paragraphs.text: Marriott’s distribution plan for 2023–2025 was to return $11.7 billion–$13.6 billion to shareholders, and the cash bridge records $13,002 million. That fulfilled the promise, but the payments were larger than internally generated cash. The difference could come from existing cash, asset sales or borrowing, each of which reduces future flexibility in a different way.

paragraphs.text: Debt would become a larger concern if dividends and buybacks continued to exceed cash generation through 2027–2029. That would constrain repurchases, raise interest pressure and justify a lower multiple.

blocks.heading: What is Marriott's dividend yield at today's price?

paragraphs.text: Marriott International earns fees by franchising, managing and licensing hotel brands, so its stock price values a stream of future payments from hotels and partners. At $385.71, the price assumes that stream will keep growing even though debt and other claims already stand ahead of shareholders.

Free cash flow yield is 2.2%, while real free cash flow yield is 2.0% and the dividend yield is 0.8%. A 10-year U.S. Treasury yield of 5.19% makes Marriott’s modest current cash return especially relevant.

earnings.title: Marriott earnings: guidance and results
earnings.meta_description: Marriott reports on November 2, 2026, with guidance for RevPAR and net rooms growth and a test of hotel and card fee growth.
earnings.opening: Marriott's next results are expected on November 2, 2026. The one thing to watch is whether Marriott separates hotel-related fee growth from the contribution of credit cards.
earnings.closing: The full Marriott memo also covers Marriott's business, rivals, management, and risks.

paragraphs.text: For 2026, management guides to worldwide RevPAR growth of 3.0%–3.5%. It expects net rooms growth of 4.5%–5.0%. Adjusted EBITDA guidance is $5,965–$6,025 million. Capital returns should reach at least $4,500 million.

blocks.heading: Has Marriott kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management expected approximately US$4 billion of shareholder distributions on August 5, 2025, and ultimately reported more than US$4 billion. A September 2023 presentation modeled 2025 adjusted EBITDA of US$5.2–5.7 billion; the eventual result was US$5.38 billion. Marriott therefore delivered on those stated targets, but shareholders still must judge the prices paid for buybacks, the cost of equity awards and the debt used to support distributions. The fairest conclusion is conditional: Marriott’s managers have reasons to align with shareholders, while the board and investors must keep testing how well that alignment survives financing and succession decisions.

blocks.heading: What is Marriott's revenue and profit trend?

paragraphs.text: Revenue rose to $7,071 million from $6,744 million. Operating income slipped from $1,236 million to $1,229 million, while net income edged from $763 million to $766 million. EPS rose from $2.78 to $2.90 because fewer shares gave each remaining share a larger claim on earnings.

Cash improved as well. Operating cash flow reached $948 million from $643 million. Free cash flow was $796 million from $488 million. The eight-quarter record remains uneven, so the strongest reading is stronger underlying fees and cash, not yet a completely settled profit trend.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Marriott's next release?

paragraphs.text: Marriott will report third-quarter results on November 2, 2026. The release is scheduled for approximately 7 a.m. Eastern, followed by an 8 a.m. conference call. Investors will test the RevPAR and adjusted-EPS ranges shown above, while separating hotel-related fee growth from the contribution of credit cards.
